verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The explicit Faa di Bruno expansion of the display — the sum over compositions I_1+...+I_n = I with coefficients c_{I_1,...,I_n} and the factor y_sigma^{1/2-n} — occurs nowhere in the Lean; no declaration forms it, and the repository contains no Faa di Bruno / OrderedFinpartition machinery at all. The Lean reaches the same destination (the derivative bound of the next display) by two norm-level routes instead. Route one: `comp_jet_bound` wraps Mathlib's norm_iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_le, which is the quantitative shadow of the same combinatorics, and feeds it the one-dimensional outer-derivative identity `iteratedDeriv_rpow` (d^n/dt^n t^p = rpowCoeff p n * t^{p-n}); at p = 1/2 that supplies exactly the paper's y^{1/2-n} factor, but only inside a norm estimate, with the composition combinatorics collapsed into the factor n.factorial. Route two: `sqrt_class` avoids the composition entirely, writing sqrt(g) = 2 * (g / (2 sqrt g)) and invoking a signed-quotient class lemma. The paper uses the display only to derive the next bound, which both routes prove, so the surrounding result is not affected.
